actions.justification: Mandatory first step - assess HR, BP, SpO2, RR for baseline and continuous monitoring. Vitals show HR 100, BP 130/80, SpO2 95%, RR 22 - tachycardia and mildly reduced SpO2 warrant close monitoring.
Class I mandatory action per AHA guidelines - 12-lead ECG must be obtained and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact to confirm STEMI and guide emergent reperfusion therapy.

Mandatory initial assessment - characterize chest pain onset, duration, radiation, associated symptoms, and risk factors to support STEMI diagnosis and risk stratification. Also document aspirin/NSAID allergy which is critical for treatment planning.

MANDATORY: Immediate cath lab activation is required for primary PCI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes. Patient is at 15 minutes since arrival - must activate now to meet the 90-minute benchmark.

MANDATORY: P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) loading dose is required for STEMI. This is NOT an aspirin/NSAID and is safe despite the documented aspirin/NSAID allergy. Critical adjunctive antiplatelet therapy for STEMI per AHA guidelines.
MANDATORY: Anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin or enoxaparin is required as adjunctive therapy for STEMI prior to PCI per AHA Class I guidelines. Must be administered promptly.

Primary PCI is the definitive reperfusion strategy for STEMI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes; patient is at 30 minutes. Cath lab is activated — arranging PCI now is critical to meet the time target.
IV access is essential for medication administration, contrast delivery during PCI, and emergency drug delivery. Required for ongoing STEMI management.
Patient's SpO2 is 95%, which is at the lower threshold. Supplemental oxygen is indicated to maintain SpO2 ≥94% in STEMI patients with hypoxia per AHA guidelines.

MANDATORY action for STEMI. CRITICAL SAFETY NOTE: Patient has documented aspirin/NSAID allergy — clinical team must review allergy severity (anaphylaxis vs. intolerance) before administration. If true anaphylaxis, aspirin is contraindicated and alternative antiplatelet strategy should be confirmed. P2Y12 inhibitor (already given) remains essential. If allergy is mild/intolerance, aspirin may still be given under physician oversight per ACC/AHA guidelines for STEMI.

High-sensitivity troponin should be obtained at presentation per AHA guidelines for STEMI workup. Labs are currently pending — confirming troponin result supports diagnosis and baseline for monitoring myocardial injury extent.

Cardiology consult is essential for lateral STEMI management, coordination with cath lab team, and guidance on aspirin allergy management in the context of dual antiplatelet therapy requirements for primary PCI.
Formal ECG interpretation of the 12-lead confirming lateral STEMI pattern, extent of ST elevation, and any additional findings to guide ongoing management.

Patient has severe crushing chest pain with HR 100 and RR 22, suggesting significant pain/anxiety. Morphine can reduce pain and sympathetic activation. Note: aspirin allergy documented but morphine is appropriate for pain management in STEMI.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (BP 130/80, HR 100, SpO2 95%). Beta-blocker is indicated per AHA guidelines for STEMI to reduce myocardial oxygen demand and heart rate, provided no contraindications (no evidence of cardiogenic shock, bradycardia, or active bronchospasm).

Patient has lateral STEMI with ongoing chest pain and adequate BP (130/80). This is not an inferior STEMI, so RV infarction is not a primary concern. Nitrates are indicated for symptom relief. Aspirin allergy noted but nitrates are not contraindicated here.
Comparison with prior ECG can help characterize the extent and acuity of ST changes, assist with risk stratification, and provide baseline for post-PCI comparison.

Patient is at 85 minutes since arrival with door-to-balloon target of <90 minutes. If PCI cannot be completed within the 90-minute window, fibrinolysis should be considered as a backup reperfusion strategy per AHA guidelines. This is a critical time-sensitive decision point.
